title: Responsive vs fixed layouts
learningObjectives: Explain responsive vs fixed layouts and apply responsive design principles.

understand.concept: A fixed layout uses rigid dimensions that may not adapt to the available space. A responsive layout adjusts structure and sizing to suit different viewport widths, content lengths, and user settings. Flexible grids, intrinsic sizing, and media queries are common tools.
understand.whyItMatters: Fixed widths can cause horizontal scrolling or clipped content on small screens. Responsive design supports a wider range of devices, languages, and text sizes.
understand.analogy: A fixed layout is like furniture bolted to one room size; a responsive layout can rearrange to fit different rooms.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; responsive behaviour is determined by CSS layout and viewport/container conditions.

explain.narrative: The layout uses two columns on wider screens and one column at a narrow breakpoint.

examples.explanation: The layout uses two columns on wider screens and one column at a narrow breakpoint.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered example showing the responsive behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Build a page with a fixed-width version, then refactor it using flexible sizing and a media query. Compare overflow.
practise.independentTask: Build a responsive page section and test it at narrow, medium, and wide viewport sizes, including longer labels.
hints: Use the browser responsive viewport tools.
Check horizontal overflow and text scaling.
Keep keyboard access and semantic structure intact.
